issues.issue: Was the Immigration Division's hearing procedurally fair (abandoned para 51(b) allegation, alleged bias, and erroneous mention of an appeal right)?
issues.applicant_position: ID pursued an abandoned para 51(b) ground, acted as co-counsel showing bias, and wrongly said she could appeal; higher fairness was required.
issues.result_text: Applicant has not shown the ID breached procedural fairness; bias and appeal-right mention did not cause unfairness.

issues.issue: Was the ID's finding of inadmissibility for misrepresentation (withholding marriage) reasonable?
issues.applicant_position: No specific IRPA or regulation provision on timing of disclosure; she was candid at entry, so withholding cannot be rationalized.
issues.result_text: ID decision meets the reasonableness standard; failure to disclose marriage breached duty of candour under the Regulations.

issues.issue: Did the IAD lack jurisdiction because the visa had expired before the Exclusion Order was issued?
issues.applicant_position: Visa was valid when the reports were issued; McLeod and Ismail show no statutory need for an unexpired visa.
issues.result_text: Subsection 63(2) applies only to current visa holders; IAD could reasonably find no jurisdiction.

issues.issue: Should costs be awarded on a solicitor-client basis?
issues.applicant_position: Seeks solicitor-client costs in further memorandums.
issues.result_text: No special reasons shown under Federal Courts Rules s. 22 to depart from the general no-costs rule.

issues.issue: Should the proposed certified questions on disclosure and visa validity timing be certified?
issues.applicant_position: Two questions should be certified on the disclosure obligation and timing of visa validity.
issues.respondent_position: Questions do not meet the certification test.
issues.result_text: First question refused as fact-specific; a rephrased question on visa validity timing certified in IMM-6270-19 only.
